intro: This week’s digest highlights major moves in satellite internet and AI, with Amazon’s $10.8 billion acquisition of Globalstar and Cerebras’ IPO filing signaling shifts in tech infrastructure. Retail and luxury sectors face evolving challenges as soaring gold prices impact jewelry margins, while DoorDash and Signet Jewelers adjust strategies to capture new market opportunities.

readOneThing.title: Amazon Buys Globalstar for $10.8 Billion, Movingto Expand Its Satellite Internet Service

items.title: Amazon Buys Globalstar for $10.8 Billion, Movingto Expand Its Satellite Internet Service
bullets: The deal includes a partnership with Apple to enable Amazon’s satellites to connect with iPhones and Apple Watches for emergency texting features starting in 2028.
Amazon's Project Kuiper, recently renamed Leo, launched its first 27 satellites last April to compete with SpaceX’s Starlink in providing high-speed internet from low-Earth orbit.

items.title: Fashion Briefing: Gold prices are skyrocketing, squeezing the jewelry industry’s margins in uncomfortable ways
bullets: Gold prices surged past $4,900 in January 2026, briefly reaching $5,500, driven by inflation and Middle East tensions.
Jewelry brand Ring Concierge raised prices by about 10% due to gold costs now comprising 60% of material expenses.
The rising gold price trend has persisted over the past year, with forecasts suggesting it could exceed $6,000 by year-end.

items.title: AI chip startup Cerebras files for IPO
bullets: Cerebras Systems, an AI chip startup, has filed for an initial public offering planned for mid-May after a previous attempt was delayed and withdrawn. The company reported $510 million in revenue and a net income of $237.8 million in 2025, with a non-GAAP net loss of $75.7 million excluding one-time items. Cerebras recently secured deals with Amazon Web Services and OpenAI, with the latter reportedly worth more than $10 billion, and raised over $2 billion in funding rounds at a $23 billion valuation.

items.title: Airwallex Takes Its Cross-Border Play In-Store
bullets: Airwallex launched an in-store point-of-sale system enabling merchants to accept cross-border in-person payments through a single platform. The company holds nearly 90 regulatory licenses across about 50 markets and connects to local payment networks in over 100 countries. Merchants expanding internationally face operational challenges like onboarding local acquirers and managing vendor relationships, which Airwallex aims to simplify with its global infrastructure.

items.title: Slow revenue conversion to dog IT companies as AI queers the pitch
bullets: Tata Consultancy Services and Wipro experienced declines in annual revenue despite increases in their total contract values due to slow revenue conversion and AI-driven discounts.
TCS reported a 2.4% drop in constant currency annual revenue for FY26, while Wipro posted a 1.6% decline, marking its third consecutive year of revenue decrease.
Contract values for application development and management services fell by 20% in Q1 2026, with managed services contract values declining for three consecutive quarters amid pricing pressures.

items.title: Signet Jewelers repositions H. Samuel and Ernest Jones within the watch market
bullets: Signet Jewelers has repositioned Ernest Jones away from the luxury watch segment to focus on a mid-market range featuring brands like Longines, Tissot, and Rado.
In 2023, Signet sold 19 Ernest Jones stores, including 14 multibrand showrooms and five monobrand boutiques, to exit the prestige watch market.
Since Neil Old became managing director in 2019, Signet has accelerated digital improvements, rightsized its store estate, and shifted its UK watch strategy amid pandemic and economic challenges.

items.title: Marketplace Briefing: How DoorDash is winning over apparel brands
bullets: DoorDash expanded its marketplace in late March by adding apparel brands Urban Outfitters, Steve Madden, Dolce Vita, and Rally House to its delivery platform.
In the fourth quarter, DoorDash's gross order value increased 39% year over year, reaching an expected $31 billion to $31.8 billion by March.
DoorDash currently partners with over 150,000 non-restaurant retailers, up from 115,000 in 2024, and has been developing its retail delivery services for about five years.
